findings.title: Remote mode can't finish a round trip for the only user: every phone edit and pick waits on the desktop twice
findings.claim: KICKOFF says the person is the only user, so in practice every Artifact viewer is the owner. The design never applies the owner's inbox rows. Each one becomes a desktop card with Yes pre-selected, and getting that far already needs a person at the desktop to run /room sync (ArtifactData goes through the normal permission flow). So nothing done on the phone takes effect until the person is back at the computer and confirms it a second time. The Send to Claude wake can't close the gap either: import needs the person key, and the mod passes that key only on presses, submits and a typed /room. A wake is none of those. Either the wake can't import, or the mod runs import with the person key with no person present, which breaks the actor rules.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Remote mode step 5: "A row under the owner's own uid ... applies nothing ... They become one card the local person confirms: 'Apply 3 edits and 1 pick from your phone?', with Yes pre-selected." Step 7: "live/head shows it as waiting until the local person confirms." Step 6: "the mod runs /room sync" on a wake, while step 5 runs import "with the person key, as part of the person's command", and Person actions say the key is passed "only" on presses, submits and typed /room. Conflicts with KICKOFF context ("I'm the only user"), R13 (Artifact "for when localhost isn't reachable"), principle 1 ("one tap to confirm"; never ask twice), and the S11 evidence path in feature_list.json ("a phone edit is made in it; /room sync imports it as an attributed user edit"). The S11 CI path passes only because it uses a non-owner viewer u_test ("u_test is not the owner").
findings.failure_scenario: The owner is away from the laptop, opens the Artifact on a phone, taps the pre-selected pick on a card and renames a block. Both show as queued for good. Pressing Send to Claude wakes the session, but import can't run as a person, so nothing lands. Back at the desk, the owner runs /room sync, may get an ArtifactData permission prompt, and then has to confirm "Apply 1 edit and 1 pick from your phone?". The S11 evidence run, done by the owner, records a confirmation card rather than an attributed user edit. And since Yes is pre-selected on rows the model could have forged, the card gets rubber-stamped and protects nothing.
findings.proposed_fix: Pair the owner's device so its rows can be authenticated without the model seeing the key. The pane (not model-visible) or the local canvas tab shows a short pairing code once. The page stores it in its own localStorage and puts an HMAC over each inbox row, keyed by a secret derived from the code. import checks the HMAC against a hash kept with the person key in the mod's $.store. Paired owner rows then apply directly as person:artifact:<uid> (device-attributed), and only unpaired owner rows fall back to the card, with No pre-selected. State explicitly that a wake-triggered sync imports only other viewers' rows and paired rows. Add an S11 CI step with an owner-uid paired row.

findings.title: The canvas has no designed way to edit by hand: regroup, rename, re-wire, forbid, hide, pin
findings.claim: R6 requires that the map can be shaped by hand on the canvas. The canvas design lists views, transports, motion and gestures, but no direct-manipulation editing. Nothing says how a person regroups two blocks, renames one, adds or forbids an intended relation, hides noise or pins a position. On the phone, a one-finger drag pans, so dragging a block has no defined meaning there. The desktop layout itself is never specified; only the 390 px layout is.
findings.evidence: architecture.md The canvas: Views and the Writes bullet ("An edit is applied optimistically") never name an edit control. design-language.md Touch gesture table: "Drag with one finger on the felt | pans", tap selects, long press opens evidence. No gesture or control for group, move, rename, relate, forbid, hide or pin, though the CLI has all of them (architecture.md The CLI, `edit OP`). KICKOFF R6 ("shaped by hand on the canvas or by asking Claude: regroup, rename, re-scope, re-wire, hide noise, pin a layout"). The S4 evidence path (feature_list.json) needs "the regroup and intended change on the canvas ... at 1440x900 and 390x844". S8 evidence has the tab renaming. S15 needs every top-level control tagged with one of the five data-concepts.
findings.failure_scenario: Running the S4 evidence: the person opens the canvas to regroup storefront cart and checkout under 'purchase' and forbid worker→orders-db. No control exists, so they fall back to /room edit in the terminal, and the canvas S4 evidence and R6 'by hand' can't be produced. If implementers invent controls during the build, they risk a sixth top-level concept that fails exactly_five_concepts, or a drag that clashes with the pan gesture on the phone.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an 'Edit by hand' section to design-language.md and architecture.md. The selected block gets a small action tray under Levels or Intent (rename, group with…, hide, pin), each running a catalogue `edit` leaf. On desktop, dragging a block onto another block's lid regroups it (`edit move`), and a drag on empty felt pins the block. Shift-drag from block to block draws chalk to make an intended relation, and the relation's popover offers Forbid. On phone, long press opens evidence plus the same action tray in the bottom sheet, and 'Move into…' is picked from a list rather than dragged. Specify the desktop layout (rail, tray, stack and board positions). Add Playwright tests for each edit at 1440 and 390, plus undo.

findings.title: A canvas reload loses its login, and the pending edits saved for the reload can never be sent
findings.claim: The bearer token lives only in the tab's memory, so a reload leaves the tab unauthenticated. The only way back in, `e` or `/room open`, opens a new tab. sessionStorage belongs to one tab, so the pending edits the design keeps there 'to survive a reload' stay in the orphaned tab and are never sent. serve also binds a random port on each start, so after serve restarts (idle exit after 30 min, a drain on a version change, a reboot) the origin changes and the old origin's storage can't be reached at all. Nothing defines what the reloaded, unauthenticated tab shows.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Local server Auth: "the tab keeps [the token] in memory ... A reload asks for a new code: e or /room open"; `open` "opens http://127.0.0.1:PORT/#code=... in the browser itself"; `serve` "binds 127.0.0.1:0". The canvas Writes bullet: "Pending edits survive a reload in sessionStorage ... until confirmed [DR-8]". The empty_state_audit visits views on an empty workspace, not an unauthenticated tab. Conflicts with principle 1 ("Never lose or overwrite what someone did"; "Never show a blank state") and S8 (no write is lost).
findings.failure_scenario: serve is draining for a newer engine, or the laptop just woke. The person renames a block and regroups two more, and the edits sit pending. They reload the tab: it has no token, so the edits can't be sent, and the page shows an error or a blank. They press `e`, which opens a fresh tab on a possibly different port with empty sessionStorage. The three edits are gone for good, and the old tab still holds them where nothing will ever flush them.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the bearer token in sessionStorage, which is scoped by origin and port and so out of reach of other local servers, so a reload within one serve stays logged in. Make serve prefer a stable port per workspace, recorded in serve.json and tried first, so the origin survives a restart. Keep pending edits in localStorage keyed by workspace_id and have any authenticated tab of that workspace flush them with their original idem. Give the unauthenticated tab an engine-authored empty state ('This tab needs a fresh link: press e in the pane') that keeps showing the pending count. Add e2e tests: reload with pending edits, then serve restarting with pending edits.

findings.title: `e` and /room open claim success where localhost can't be reached (cloud, SSH, remote surfaces)
findings.claim: `planroom open` always launches a browser on the engine's machine and prints "opened in browser". Nothing checks whether that machine has a display, or whether the person is attached from a remote surface. In a cloud container like this build's, over SSH, or from the Claude mobile or web surface, nothing opens, yet the person is told it did, and the pane never points them to /room share, which the design reserves for exactly this case.
findings.evidence: architecture.md The CLI: `open` "starts serve if needed and opens the canvas in the browser ... prints 'opened in browser'". The pane's `e` key and the Fallback panes have no 'no display' state. mod-spike: "A cloud session with no app attached: session.start reports surface: null"; mod-api: remote surfaces join through session.attach. KICKOFF R13: the canvas "is also published as a Claude Artifact for when localhost isn't reachable". KICKOFF context: the environment is a cloud Claude Code container. Principle 1: "Never ask what a good default could answer."
findings.failure_scenario: The owner drives a cloud session from claude.ai on a laptop and presses `e`. The engine runs xdg-open inside the container, which fails or opens nothing, and the line reads "opened in browser". No canvas appears, and nothing suggests `t` or /room share. The person concludes the canvas is broken.
findings.proposed_fix: Have `open` detect when there's no reachable local browser: no DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY on Linux, SSH_CONNECTION set, a container marker, an opener that exits non-zero, or the mod seeing a remote or mobile surface. It then returns an engine-authored empty state whose next action is `/room share` ('This machine has no browser you can see; share the canvas to your phone instead?'). The pane and band offer that on the same key. Add `first_run.rs::open_without_a_display_offers_share`.

findings.title: No band on vscode or mobile, and the pane has no row for the next action
findings.claim: The band carries PaneModel.next, but the band exists only on the terminal and desktop surfaces. The pane's sections don't include a next-action row, so on vscode and mobile the R13 'next best action' isn't shown when no decision is open.
findings.evidence: mod-api.md item 9: "The band is terminal and desktop only." architecture.md Pane table: focus, decision, progress, diffs, drift, who, mini-map, list, with no `next` row; "Mobile has no band, Input or Select". contracts.md PaneModel.next: "the band's next best action". R13 asks for the next best action.
findings.failure_scenario: In the Claude mobile app attached to a session, with no open decision, the pane shows focus, progress and diffs but no suggested action. The person has to guess what to do next.
findings.proposed_fix: When the surface has no band (or no decision is open), draw PaneModel.next as the face-up card in the decision section, as the canvas already does. Assert it in no_blank_pane on all four surfaces.

findings.title: Band digits swallow the first character of a message and act as the person
findings.claim: Because a bare digit at the empty prompt presses the band, a person can't start a message with 1, 2 or 3 while the band is shown. The digit is eaten and runs a person-actor command such as accepting a ghost or picking a decision. It's reversible, but the person's keystroke is lost and an action they didn't mean is recorded as theirs, with no undo shown.
findings.evidence: mod-spike: "A bare digit at the empty prompt presses the mod's band Button." architecture.md Band: "so a stray digit at the start of a message must never do harm"; DR-54 rejected a confirmation. S9 requires two keys from pane focus, not one key from the prompt. Principle 1: "Never lose or overwrite what someone did."
findings.failure_scenario: The person types "1. retry on 503s". The `1` accepts Claude's two pending edits as the person, and the message arrives as ". retry on 503s".
findings.proposed_fix: After any band press from the prompt, show a toast with the engine-authored line and 'u undo', and make the next keystroke an undo. Alternatively, give band Buttons no digit hotkeys and bind the primary through an engine keybinding `action`, reaching the rest through ctrl+x tab, which S9 still allows.

findings.title: A four-choice decision card doesn't fit its 6-row budget at 49 columns
findings.claim: The decision section is budgeted at 6 rows but holds a question line, a why line, 2 to 4 choices and a '+N more' line. That's 7 rows with 4 stacked choices. Putting 4 Buttons side by side at 49 columns leaves about 11 columns per engine-authored label.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Pane table: "6 | The one decision: a one-line question, a one-line why, 2 to 4 choices with the pick marked, '+N more'". contracts.md DecisionCard.choices "2 to 4". mod-spike measured a 6-row card with three Buttons only.
findings.failure_scenario: A four-choice card pushes the list below its 10-row minimum and fails rows_fit_at_49x34. Or the labels truncate to unreadable stubs, and the person opens detail just to understand the choices.
findings.proposed_fix: Cap pane-visible choices at 3 and put the rest behind '+more', or lay them out 2×2 with a label budget per choice in en.toml. Make rows_fit_at_49x34 use a 4-choice card and assert that no label is cut.

findings.title: The pane is undefined below 110 columns and the 49-column dock
findings.claim: The pane opens unasked only on fullscreen viewports of 110 columns or more, and is designed only for 49×34. What /room shows on an 80 to 100 column terminal (a split pane, a laptop) isn't specified, and the dock there would be narrower than the design's minimum.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Wiring step 5 ("at least 110 columns") and Pane ("designed for 49×34, the narrowest dock"). mod-api: the dock is at most 45% of columns. The spike measured only 120×40 and 200×50.
findings.failure_scenario: On a 90-column terminal, /room opens a dock about 36 columns wide. The focus header, diff hunk and choice labels wrap or truncate, and rows_fit was never run at that size.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a compact layout for docks under 49 columns: header, card and list only, with diffs and drift behind keys. Or open the pane as an overlay when the dock would be too narrow. Run surfaces tests at 80×24 and 100×30.

findings.title: The phone's top row can't hold breadcrumb lids, search, lenses and the project shelf at 44 px
findings.claim: At 390 px the design puts the breadcrumb of stacked lids (up to 5 levels), search, the lens switcher and the project shelf in one row with 44 px targets. That's roughly 8 or more targets plus labels in about 358 px, with no collapse rule, which risks overflow or illegible labels against S13.
findings.evidence: design-language.md Touch: "puts the breadcrumb, the lens switcher and the project shelf in one row at the top ... every target is at least 44 px". architecture.md: search lives inside the breadcrumb. S13: "no overflow, tap targets of at least 44 px".
findings.failure_scenario: At code level with 2 projects and 5 lenses, the row needs about 12 targets. Either it overflows (no_overflow_at_390x844 fails) or the targets shrink below 44 px.
findings.proposed_fix: On the phone, show only the current lid plus a '⋯' lid that opens the ancestors. Make the lens switcher one swatch button that opens a sheet, and the project shelf one chip. Document the collapse rule and test it at the deepest level with several projects.

findings.title: Controls that exist only on the Artifact have no concept, and its 'Needs your computer' button can't do anything
findings.claim: The Artifact page adds Send to Claude, sync/queued status and Ask Claude/Use this. Only Ask Claude has a stated home (on a card). Send to Claude and the queued counter are top-level controls with no data-concept. The page's empty state for views it can't serve offers '/room open' as its one next-action button, which can't be pressed on a phone.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Remote mode steps 4, 6 and 7, and The canvas ("Needs your computer: open this workspace there with /room open"). design-language.md Empty states: "the single next action as a button". S15: "The UI exposes no top-level concepts beyond R14's five"; the empty-state audit runs through the Artifact page.
findings.failure_scenario: exactly_five_concepts, if run on the Artifact page, finds an untagged Send to Claude control, or it gets mis-tagged. A phone viewer taps 'open this workspace there' and nothing happens.
findings.proposed_fix: Show queued rows and Send to Claude as the face-up Decisions card ('3 changes waiting for your computer · Send now'). Give the Artifact's unavailable state an action that works on the phone, either that same send or 'remind me on my computer', which writes an inbox row the next sync turns into the band's next action.

findings.title: The pane has no key to run or jump to a plan stage
findings.claim: R5 lets the person jump between stages, and S3 walks seven stages, but no pane key runs `intent next --stage S`, lints, or tags a version. In the pane those steps need a typed /room line or an Esc back to the band, so the S3 flow from the pane leans on typing rather than the key map.
findings.evidence: architecture.md Pane table: `i` intent is the only intent key; the action keys are z x l p a o i d y n f w m s h g u e c t. The CLI's `intent next [--stage S] | lint | version LABEL`. R5: "The person can jump between stages."
findings.failure_scenario: The person opens the plan with `i`, selects the 'breakdown' row, and finds no action key to run that stage. Enter only 'opens' it, so they have to type /room intent next --stage breakdown.
findings.proposed_fix: Make Enter on a stage row in the `i` list run `intent next --stage S` (Edit-class, reversible), show lint findings as rows, and have the engine rank the version tag as the next action once a stage batch is accepted. Add S3 to main_flows_within_two_keys with no typed /room beyond the first intent.

findings.title: The light-mode card token is near-white, and it fills large panels
findings.claim: --card #f6fbf8 is effectively off-white, and it paints panels that cover much of the screen: the bottom sheet at half detent, DiffTray, PlanBoard and Anatomy. On the phone that reads as an off-white background, which KICKOFF bans.
findings.evidence: design-language.md Palette: "--card | #f6fbf8 | ... | Panels, cards"; Touch: half detent "shows the tray, the board or the whole card". KICKOFF Look and feel: "Don't use: a cream or off-white background".
findings.failure_scenario: The 390×844 screenshot critique with the half-detent sheet open shows about half the screen as near-white, which goes against the felt-table concept and the binding don't-list.
findings.proposed_fix: Tint --card into the felt family (for example #e3f1ea or a lighter mint) and re-check contrast in tokens.test.ts. Or give the sheet a felt-colored body with --card only on individual cards.

verdicts.reason: The design really does route every owner-uid inbox row into a desktop confirmation card. The owner is the only user (KICKOFF line 8) and the only viewer who can press Send to Claude, so nothing done on the phone applies until someone is at the desktop. The wake path is also left undefined: step 6 has the mod run /room sync on a wake, but import is person-only and the person key is passed only on presses, submits and typed /room. So a wake either can't import or would have to import with no person present. DR-52/DR-56 chose the owner card on purpose (owner decision D15), but they never reconcile it with the wake trigger or with the only-user reality. The S11 CI path avoids the problem only by using a non-owner u_test. I'm keeping it material: the remote round trip, a main R13/S11 flow, can't complete as designed, and that conflicts with principle 1's 'interrupt only for decisions only they can make'.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md Remote mode step 5: 'A row under the owner's own uid ... applies nothing ... one card the local person confirms ... Yes pre-selected'; step 6: 'A wake carries only "sync requested": the mod runs /room sync'; Person actions: key passed on 'A button press (onPress), an input submit (onSubmit), or a /room the person typed'; feature_list S11 asserts 'u_test is not the owner'; decisions.md:1046 'Send to Claude works for viewers with edit access, the owner among them; other viewers' rows wait for the owner's next sync'; KICKOFF:8 'I'm the only user'.

verdicts.reason: No document defines a direct-manipulation control on the canvas for group, move, rename, relate, forbid, hide or pin. The only one-finger drag on the phone pans. Yet R6 requires shaping by hand on the canvas, the S4 evidence needs a canvas regroup and intended change, and S11 CI and S8 assume the page or tab can rename. The only map write the canvas names is the evidence popover's Confirm/Reject running review. Anatomy has 'part editing', but only for breakdowns. A required capability is undesigned on the surface R6 names, and invented controls risk failing exactly_five_concepts or clashing with the gestures, so it stays material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md The canvas: Views list and 'Writes. ... An edit is applied optimistically as pending' name no edit control; 'An evidence popover's Confirm and Reject run review'. design-language.md Touch table: 'Drag with one finger on the felt | pans'. KICKOFF R6 'shaped by hand on the canvas ... regroup, rename, re-scope, re-wire, hide noise, pin a layout'. feature_list S4 evidence: 'the regroup and intended change on the canvas ... at 1440x900 and 390x844'; S11 CI: 'the viewer renames storefront:dir:src/cart in the page'.

verdicts.reason: The finding holds. The bearer token lives only in tab memory, so a reloaded tab can't send anything, and the only way back in (e or /room open) opens a fresh tab, which gets its own sessionStorage. The reloaded tab keeps its pending edits, but it can never authenticate, because the code goes only to the newly opened URL. serve binds port 0 and exits after 30 idle minutes or on drain, so a restart changes the origin as well. The claim 'Pending edits survive a reload in sessionStorage' therefore can't deliver what it promises, and nothing defines what the unauthenticated tab shows. That is a data-loss risk against principle 1 ('Never lose ... what someone did'), so it's material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md Local server Auth: 'the tab keeps [the token] in memory ... A reload asks for a new code: e or /room open'; 'opens http://127.0.0.1:PORT/#code=... in the browser itself'; 'planroom serve binds 127.0.0.1:0'; Processes table: serve 'exits after 30 min with no client, or when an engine of another version ... asks it to drain'; The canvas Writes: 'Pending edits survive a reload in sessionStorage ... until confirmed [DR-8]'; decisions.md:552 'a reload of the tab asks for a new code, one e press'.

verdicts.reason: The gap is real. No document handles a machine with no display or a remote surface for `open`: it always claims 'opened in browser', and the mod-spike shows cloud sessions with surface: null. It isn't material, though. No tier A or B scenario depends on `e` working without a display: S4 and S13 drive the canvas with Playwright, and S11 uses /room share. Remote mode stays reachable through the pane's `t` key and /room share. This is a misleading message and a missed default, not a scenario failure, a data-loss risk or a security risk.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md CLI: open 'starts serve if needed and opens the canvas in the browser ... prints "opened in browser"'; Pane list keys include 't remote'; '/room share and /room sync wrap share and import'; mod-spike: 'session.start reports surface: null'; no grep hit for DISPLAY, xdg or 'no browser' in the design docs; feature_list S13 and S4 evidence use Playwright, and S11 uses share.

verdicts.reason: Real and minor. The phone's single top row holds the breadcrumb of lids (with search inside it), the lens switcher and the project shelf, every target at least 44 px, and no collapse rule is given for deep levels or several projects.
